Ce reportage a pris forme lorsque Lela,: This story took shape when Lela, our editor-in-chief, asked me to look into the situation of a family whose refugee claim had been rejected. For them, the next step was to apply for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
Ce processus est coûteux pour les famill: The process is expensive for low-income families, and this story explores how applying under the humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) considerations category is the last resort for many immigrants and asylum seekers who hope to stay in Canada. Yet it is a lifeline that few people can hold on to.

To my surprise, the person guiding others through the maze of the system was facing the same obstacles as the people who came to her for help.
Des décisions arbitraires, une forte dem: Arbitrary decisions, high demand for immigration programs and mounting backlogs are pushing international students, foreign workers and refugees to apply under the humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) considerations category as a last resort to stay in Canada. However, few of them get a favourable decision, because many obstacles stand in their way.
Angie Sanchez est arrivée à Montréal en: Angie Sanchez arrived in Montréal in September 2022 as an international student, with her husband and their two children. They decided to leave Colombia, their home country, to find a place where their children could grow up safely.
« D’abord, c’est pour la sécurité des en: “First, it was for the children’s safety. That was the main factor. Then, because we wanted to change our way of life, to have a calmer life – less stress and chaos – and finally, because we wanted to interact with different kinds of people,” says Ms.<sup></sup> Sanchez.
Avant d’émigrer, elle et son mari envisa: Before emigrating, she and her husband considered Spain or the United States in addition to Canada, because they have family in those countries.
« Lorsque nous réfléchissions à différen: “When we were thinking about different options for leaving the country, we wanted to find a way to do it properly, legally. At that time, Canada, with its student program, was the option that appealed to us most,” says Ms.<sup></sup> Sanchez.
Ce qui était intéressant, pour Angie et: What appealed to Angie and her family was that international students in Canada can study while working up to 24 hours a week off campus. They are also allowed to bring their children, who can continue their schooling, and their spouse or common-law partner, who can work full time for any employer in Canada with an open work permit.
Après avoir pris la décision de venir à: After deciding to come to Montréal, Angie Sanchez applied for a study permit, a federal document that allows foreign nationals to study at designated learning institutions. She planned to become a legal assistant and, eventually, to apply for permanent residence with her family. “We saw more possibilities for the future here,” she says.
Pendant ses études, elle a demandé une p: While she was studying, she applied to extend her study permit. However, because of delays at Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), Angie and her family now find themselves without status. Their last resort to stay in Canada was to apply for permanent residence under the humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) considerations category.

To meet the requirements for applying for permanent residence, including the minimum of 1,800 hours of study, she had to take a training program, a professional specialization certificate (ASP).
Un an après son arrivée au Canada, Angie: A year after arriving in Canada, Angie Sanchez was already working as a community immigration worker at the Centre d’orientation parajuridique et sociale pour immigrants (COPSI), a non-profit organization in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie that offers services to low-income immigrants and refugees, particularly those from Latin America.
Elle a trouvé l’offre dans une publicati: She found the job posting in a Facebook post from COPSI saying the centre was looking for a French- and Spanish-speaking community immigration officer. Since her legal secretary studies were related to the field of immigration, she applied for the vacant position.
« J’ai fini par travailler dans ce domai: “I ended up working in this field, or rather, I stayed in community work, because my mother in Colombia worked her whole life in social services, the community sector, and so on. So I’ve been very involved in this kind of work all my life,” she says.
Son travail au COPSI consiste notamment: Her work at COPSI involves, among other things, supporting and helping people with their immigration applications.

« Selon le site Web [de l’IRCC], lorsque: “According to [IRCC’s] website, when I submitted my application, it took 180 days to get a response. That 180-day period ended on December 23, 2024, and on that date I still hadn’t received an answer,” she continues. “I called immigration services, I sent online forms, and all they told me was, ‘Wait. You have to wait.’ They always told me everything was fine, everything was in order, I just had to wait.”
Elle téléphonait quotidiennement à IRCC: She phoned IRCC every day to check on the status of her application. During one of those calls, an employee told her that her file would be reviewed by a supervisor because of the delay.
Sept mois après avoir déposé sa demande: Seven months after submitting her study permit extension application, Angie Sanchez received a letter in February 2025 from her school, the École des métiers de l’informatique, du commerce et de l’administration (EMICA), informing her that she could not continue her studies because her study permit had already expired. She was supposed to finish her studies in March 2025.
M<sup>me</sup> Sanchez a également deman: Ms.<sup></sup> Sanchez also applied to extend her Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ), because it was going to expire before she could finish her studies. It is a provincial immigration document required of international students and workers who intend to live temporarily in Quebec. When renewing the CAQ, international students must submit a new study permit application.
Huit mois après avoir demandé la prolong: Eight months after applying to extend her study permit, Angie Sanchez received a letter from IRCC informing her that her application had been rejected because her CAQ had expired.
« C’était vraiment frustrant. Après huit: “It was really frustrating. After eight months and eight days, just as my CAQ had expired, I got a response. Their decision was based solely on that,” says Ms.<sup></sup> Sanchez.
Elle a dû arrêter de travailler au COPSI: She had to stop working at COPSI because she lost her status as an international student. Her husband also lost his work permit, because it was tied to Angie’s application, as she was the principal applicant. Their children also lost their study permits.
Après avoir demandé le rétablissement du: After asking for her family’s status to be restored, she received another negative response. In the letter IRCC sent her, it said they could not verify her letter of acceptance (LOA) with her school, a document confirming that a student has been accepted at a Canadian institution. This, despite the fact that she had been enrolled at the École des métiers de l’informatique, du commerce et de l’administration (EMICA) until her study permit expired—and had been forced to interrupt her studies.
Le 28 août 2025, Angie Sanchez et sa fam: On August 28, 2025, Angie Sanchez and her family applied for permanent residence under the humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) considerations category.
« Il y a eu des erreurs administratives: “There were administrative errors in my immigration file from the very start. When I say ‘from the very start,’ I mean from the moment I made my first visa application,” she continues. “When I first applied for a student visa from my home country, I received a rejection letter, and then half an hour later I received another letter [from IRCC] saying: ‘We apologize, this was a mistake, please send us your passport.’”
Actuellement, Angie Sanchez et sa famill: Right now, Angie Sanchez and her family are living off their savings, which will soon run out. While waiting for a response to her application, she volunteers at COPSI, where she helps immigrants and refugees get their immigration documents.
« Je fais du bénévolat parce que c’est u: “I volunteer because it’s a personal commitment. I like doing it, I like helping people, because I realized that many of them face the language barrier when they look for help, and that often, hiring an immigration lawyer is expensive and they can’t afford to pay,” says Ms.<sup></sup> Sanchez.
Comme elle, de nombreux étudiants intern: Like her, many international students, foreign workers and asylum seekers apply for permanent residence on humanitarian grounds. In the case of graduates and foreign workers, many do not meet the requirements to apply for permanent residence through other immigration programs, such as Express Entry, which assigns each person a score based on their level of education, language skills, work experience and abilities, among other factors.
De plus en plus d’immigrants et de réfug: More and more immigrants and refugees who want to stay in Canada are applying for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, because immigration programs like Express Entry or the Quebec Experience Program (PEQ) are highly competitive due to heavy demand and strict eligibility criteria. Immigration applications in nearly every permanent or temporary residence category have also seen a higher <l1>refusal</l1> rate since 2023.
Dans leur demande soumise dans la catégo: In their H&C applications, applicants must present sufficient reasons that might stir the compassion of the immigration officers who decide whether they deserve to stay in Canada or not.
« Comment éveiller la compassion ? deman: “How do you stir compassion?” asks Deana Okun-Nachoff, principal lawyer at Evolution Immigration Law Group. “It’s something rather nebulous.”
L’avocate explique que les demandes dans: The lawyer explains that humanitarian and compassionate applications are not subject to a list of criteria, unlike other immigration programs, such as Express Entry. Decisions on humanitarian applications are subjective.
Comme l’ont établi des décisions judicia: As established by previous court decisions, the H&C applications that should be approved are those that would move “the average Canadian citizen and [lead them] to try to relieve [the] suffering,” says <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff, who has more than 20 years of experience in the field of immigration.
Cependant, l’augmentation du nombre de d: However, the rise in asylum claims and the stiff competition in other immigration streams are leaving many people without status in the country, ultimately pushing them to apply under the humanitarian and compassionate considerations category.
« C’est comme la dernière bouée de sauve: “It’s like the last lifeline an immigrant in Canada has when there are no other immigration options available,” says Angie Sanchez.

En 2024, le Canada a considérablement ré: In 2024, Canada significantly reduced the number of people who can submit an H&C application. The <l1>2025-2027 Immigration Levels Plan</l1> aims to “stabilize overall immigration levels and better manage migration programs,” as IRCC puts it.
In 2024, IRCC received 13,750 H&C applications. Angie Sanchez’s case is among the 10,000 that IRCC will have received in 2025. That number will keep dropping over the next two years. It will fall to 6,900 next year, then to 4,300 in 2027.
Comme l’explique M<sup>e</sup> Okun-Nach: As <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff explains, there is also a limit to the number of applications immigration officers can approve each year, which increases the likelihood of a refusal.
« Cela signifie que la liste d’attente e: “It means the waiting list is extremely long, and now, with the low quotas of people processed each year, the wait is even longer. So you’re looking at six or seven years between filing an application and getting a theoretical answer,” says Mary Foster, a community organizer with Solidarity Across Borders, a network that defends migrants’ rights.
Le temps d’attente plus long est égaleme: The longer wait is also due to the immigration department’s current strategy of cutting its workforce by about a quarter over the next three years in order to reduce spending and return to pre-pandemic staffing levels. On top of that, because each immigration officer is under pressure to make a decision within a short timeframe to avoid a pile-up of pending files, this can lead to hasty decisions.
M<sup>e</sup> Okun-Nachoff, qui est égal: <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff, who is also a co-host of Borderlines, a podcast on Canadian immigration law and policy, says in one episode of Borderlines that a viable humanitarian and compassionate application is one that would “<l1>make the immigration officer cry</l1>.”
« Cela pousse les gens à créer des récit: “It pushes people to create narratives about their lives, stories in which there’s a superhero who is also a victim, but who manages to rise above their victimhood to become a super-migrant, [showing] that this is why they’re good and why white Canada should let them in,” paints Ms.<sup></sup> Foster.
Un autre élément qui contribue à cette s: Another element contributing to this disastrous situation is that migrants and asylum seekers are currently subject to closer scrutiny and greater obstacles in obtaining status. The current immigration system has turned H&C applications into a competition to determine which cases deserve the most attention.
« C’est comme une course vers le bas. Be: “It’s like a race to the bottom. Many people who want to submit this type of application don’t really agree with the idea of presenting themselves as victims in order to get status, and that’s partly why many of my clients don’t want to claim refugee status, because they feel stigmatized,” says <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff.
Les demandes CH sont en hausse en raison: H&C applications are on the rise because of the many conflicts raging elsewhere in the world and the socio-economic challenges many people currently face. Add to that the cap on the number of H&C applications accepted, which makes many immigration officers harsher when reviewing applications, as <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff explains.
« La sympathie semble désormais faire dé: “Sympathy now seems to be lacking. As applications increase, resources are limited, and our sympathy for our fellow human beings tends to decrease, because human beings are selfish by nature,” laments lawyer Raj Sharma in the Borderlines episode mentioned earlier.
Pour M<sup>e</sup> Okun-Nachoff, le Cana: For <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff, Canada has gradually changed its narrative on migration. In her view, what was once a welcoming country for refugees and newcomers has now been reduced to numbers.
« On considère tout cela d’une manière b: “We look at all of this in a very strange, binary way. There’s no sophistication anymore, unlike what I used to feel. I think we’ve started playing this strange game of determining ‘who is worth more,’ which seems very Trumpian to me,” says the lawyer.
Elle raconte que, presque tous les jours: She says that almost every day, someone contacts her wanting to submit an H&C application but doesn’t meet the requirements.
« Je suis contactée par des médecins, de: “I’m contacted by doctors, nurses, climate change scientists, people with advanced university degrees, many of whom earned a high level of training in Canada, and these people don’t meet the requirements to get permanent residence,” <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff continues. “Meanwhile, Canada invites large numbers of people who may be living abroad but speak a minimum of French, and they get ahead of candidates like the ones I’ve described.”
Elle s’inquiète aussi du fait que la maj: She is also worried that most permanent residence programs focus on economic categories and leave out other migrants, such as people who arrived through initiatives like the Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET).
« Plus de 150 000 personnes ont été invi: “More than 150,000 people were invited to come, and today they have no way to get permanent residence. Meanwhile, the conflict in Ukraine continues. So what are they supposed to do?” asks <sup></sup>Okun-Nachoff.
M<sup>me</sup> Foster explique que cette: Ms.<sup></sup> Foster explains that this lack of solutions ultimately pushes people to live without status in the country after exhausting their last immigration option.
« Pour beaucoup de gens, lorsqu’ils obti: “For many people, when they finally get an answer, it’s a no. So what do they do then? They have to stay put and start from scratch, give up, or live undocumented forever,” continues the community organizer. “That’s why we’re pushing for a regularization program, because a considerable number of people are living in need. It’s an absolutely untenable situation.”
Un programme de régularisation signifier: A regularization program would mean that all immigrants and refugees in Canada would get status.
« Depuis le début, depuis plus de 20 ans: “From the beginning, for more than 20 years, we’ve been demanding status for all, which means everyone should now have permanent status,” Ms.<sup></sup> Foster reminds us. “[H&C] applications are presented as the solution to a problem that shouldn’t exist, especially since it’s an extremely complex and burdensome program that puts the entire weight on the person concerned.”
Pour avoir de meilleures chances d’obten: To have a better chance of succeeding with an H&C application, Ms.<sup></sup> Foster says it’s important to hire a lawyer. However, many immigrants can’t afford one. In this kind of situation, the average fee for an immigration lawyer is around $8,000, which is an additional obstacle for people who want to get status in Canada.
« La personne sans-papiers, par définiti: “An undocumented person, by definition, can’t afford to pay a lawyer. They’re entitled to legal aid, but it pays so little that very few lawyers, if any, now agree to take on this type of case. These applications involve an enormous amount of work. You have to gather evidence, write reports, and it takes a lot of effort to do things properly and have a chance of succeeding,” says Ms.<sup></sup> Foster.
Ceux et celles qui n’ont pas les moyens: Those who can’t afford a lawyer turn to organizations like COPSI, where employees like Angie Sanchez refer them to professionals who may be able to take on their case. “I’ve been through every step of the journey of the people who come to me here for help,” says Ms.<sup></sup> Sanchez. She knows exactly what they’re going through, as she herself waits to find out what her fate will be.
